questions.q: What problem does Spring Cloud Config solve?
o: Centralised, versioned configuration shared by many services
Faster compilation of microservices
Encrypted traffic between browsers and servers
Automatic creation of database tables
questions.w: Config lives in Git and is served to apps. Secrets still belong in a vault, not in the config repository.

questions.q: What does service discovery with Eureka or Consul give you?
o: Services look each other up by name, not fixed IPs
Pods are scaled automatically on demand
All services share a single database
One login works across every service
questions.w: Instances register on startup and send heartbeats, so callers get only live instances. On Kubernetes you can use built-in DNS instead.

questions.q: What does Spring Cloud Gateway do?
o: It routes external requests and applies filters such as auth and rate limits
It stores messages for later consumers to read
It generates documentation for every API it fronts
It replicates databases between several regions
questions.w: It is a reactive edge service built on WebFlux. Routes match on predicates (path, header) and apply filters.

questions.q: Which library is the recommended way to add circuit breakers and retries in Spring Cloud today?
o: Resilience4j
Hystrix
Ribbon
Zuul 1
questions.w: Hystrix and Ribbon are in maintenance or removed. Resilience4j offers circuit breaker, retry, rate limiter, bulkhead and time limiter.

questions.q: A declarative HTTP client for calling another service by interface is provided by:
o: OpenFeign or the Spring `RestClient` with HTTP interfaces
Spring Batch with a job and step configuration
Spring Integration channels only
`JdbcTemplate` with a prepared statement
questions.w: You write an interface with annotated methods and Spring generates the implementation, with timeouts and resilience added through configuration.

questions.q: A client calls a service with a 30-second default timeout while the service is hanging. What is the best protection?
o: Set short explicit timeouts and add a circuit breaker with a fallback
Retry immediately and without any upper limit on tries
Raise the timeout to five minutes so the call can finish
Give the caller many more threads to wait with
questions.w: Every remote call needs a timeout. Without one, slow dependencies tie up threads and cascade failures upwards.

questions.q: How does a distributed trace id help in a microservices system?
o: It links logs and spans of one request across every service
It authenticates the user inside each service
It compresses all request bodies
It balances load between instances
questions.w: Propagated in headers (W3C `traceparent`), it lets you follow one request end to end in Zipkin, Tempo or Jaeger.

questions.q: Why is client-side load balancing common with service discovery?
o: The caller picks an instance from the registry, saving a hop
It removes the need for any service instances to exist
It encrypts every single call automatically for you
It stores the results of each call in a local cache
questions.w: Spring Cloud LoadBalancer picks among registered instances. On Kubernetes the Service object does similar work server-side.
